text.p: The Turkish central bank injected 13.8 trillion lira on Friday via overnight lending at 75 percent on Friday to meet banks' cash demands.
Overnight money also traded at 74.75 percent. The central bank had lent a total of 27.1 trillion lira via overnight lending and an open market t-bill repurchase auction on Thursday.
The lira closed weaker at 94,900 to the dollar on higher dollar/mark parity and a higher central bank dollar rate for banks' foreign exchange transfers after Thursday's 94,670.

The central bank set its key dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 94,600 lira at the opening, up from 94,300 at Thursday's close. It further raised the rate to 94,800 lira in the day.

Bankers said the central bank's tight control over the currency market was once more confirmed this week as it kept its key dollar rate lower than market rates earlier in the week when banks' dollar demand rose.
But it propped up the U.S. currency in the last two days when banks sold dollars to raise cash.
Bankers said the market did not react to 1997 budgetary and economic targets unveiled by the Finance Minister today, adding that implementation would be awaited.
T-bills traded in a narrow band and yields firmed slightly.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4 firmed to 123.04 percent from Thursday's 122.86 percent. The second most active April 9 paper yielded 117.72 percent, up from yesterday's 117.31 percent average.
